label: Simplified ITB rules for demo
note: Illustrative costs for the demo. Every number here is an assumption, not a quote or a policy value; confirm eligibility and costs with the Defence Investment Agency.

personal_certification.includes: New-entrant welder seat, all-in: college welding certificate tuition (domestic $3.3K–$4.6K), CWB W47.1 welder tests, PPE/tools and a living stipend
personal_certification.note: Upper end of an estimated $10K–$25K range. Re-qualifying an experienced welder costs ~$2K–$6K (tests $299–$499, Okanagan College; median wage $28/hr, Job Bank 2025-11-19). Sources: conestogac.on.ca, fanshawec.ca, mohawkcollege.ca, okanagancollege.ca. Assumption.

apprentice_sponsorship.includes: First-year sponsorship costs excluding wages (supervision, in-school fees, tools); wage-inclusive gross ~$50K–$60K
apprentice_sponsorship.note: Illustrative per-apprentice cost; not a quote. Offsets exist but may not stack with ITB credit: Build Canada Apprenticeship Service up to $10K (fall 2026), Ontario Achievement Incentive up to $17K. Source: CAF 2009 https://www.nist.gov/system/files/documents/2024/01/03/CAF-pays.pdf ; https://www.ontario.ca/page/financial-supports-apprentices-and-sponsors

welder_upgrade.note: Informational (display only); the engine does not use this key yet.

company_w47_1.note: Company certification; welder tickets are only valid at a CWB-certified company. Informational (display only); the engine does not use this key yet.

capacity_per_trainee_hours_week.note: Production hours per week a newly certified welder or apprentice adds to a shop.

cert_package_trainees.note: Default cohort size for a certification package (one college course section).

capacity.note: Demo assumption: capacity gaps are filled by sponsoring apprentices through an Indigenous-governed training institution (10x per the ITB overview).
capacity.real_example: Six Nations Polytechnic: tuition-free 26-week welder pre-apprenticeship (example, not affiliated; informational)

trades._note: Every trade, not just welders. A gap (a missing certification, or missing capacity for a process) maps to the trade whose `certs` or `processes` list names it. The trade names the workers to train and, in `cost_cad`, the cost per trainee by ITB training category. A trade without `cost_cad` (welding) uses the `costs` block above, so the demo's TP-01 and TP-02 do not change. `categories` overrides the category a gap kind gets (default: recipient_by_gap). Every number is an assumption for the demo, not a quote; confirm eligibility with the Defence Investment Agency.

welding.label: Welding
welding.credential: CSA W47.1 welder tickets at a CWB-certified company
welding.note: Costs: costs.personal_certification and costs.apprentice_sponsorship above (the original demo numbers).

cnc_machining.label: CNC machining
cnc_machining.credential: Ontario General Machinist (429A) apprenticeship, or CNC set-up and programming upskilling
cnc_machining.note: Apprentice: first-year sponsorship excluding wages, same basis as the welding apprentice. 429A classroom fees are about $400 per level plus $400–$500 books for levels 2–3, and Ontario covers level 1 fees in 2026 (Conestoga, Mohawk). Upskilling an operator to CNC set-up and programming (college courses, exam, wage backfill): our estimate. Assumption.

electronics_assembly.label: Electronics assembly
electronics_assembly.credential: IPC J-STD-001 and IPC-A-610 Certified IPC Specialist (CIS)
electronics_assembly.note: CIS courses run about US$650–$1,500 per standard (3–4 days; ElectroSpec, Verion, Circuit Technology), plus the standard itself (about US$360). All-in per operator for both standards with wage backfill: our estimate. New-entrant seat (tuition and course fees for a new assembler): our estimate. Assumption.

cable_harness.label: Cable and harness assembly
cable_harness.note: IPC/WHMA-A-620 CIS courses run about US$650–$1,010 (ElectroSpec, STI); exam credits US$95–$165. All-in per operator with wage backfill: our estimate. New-entrant seat: our estimate. Assumption.

coatings_plating.label: Coatings and plating
coatings_plating.credential: NASF/AESF electroplating and surface finishing course, or AMPP coating application specialist (CAS)
coatings_plating.note: NASF/AESF electroplating classroom course US$1,800–$2,450 for non-members; AMPP CAS exam fees US$100–$200, included with the course. All-in with travel and wage backfill: our estimate. Nadcap accredits the company, so it is never a training package. Assumption.

quality_inspection.label: Quality inspection
quality_inspection.credential: CMM operation (for example PC-DMIS level 1) and first article inspection (AS9102)
quality_inspection.note: Catalog only: no routing requirement maps to inspection yet. PC-DMIS for CMM 101 is a 5-day course at about US$2,625–$2,884 plus a US$225 level 1 exam (Hexagon); AS9102 first article training and wage backfill: our estimate. Assumption.
